newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in newspapers on Tuesday. Most of the newspapers in the Indian capital were not published on Tuesday as their offices were closed on Monday for the spring festival of Holi.
DEVE GOWDA IN MOSCOW TO SIGN SEVERAL ACCORDS

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda arrived in Moscow on a three-day official visit. India and Russia are expected to sign a number of bilateral documents including a treaty on avoidance of double taxation, an agreement on plant protection and quarantine, an accord on cooperation in physical culture and sports, an extradition treaty, a treaty on mutual assistance in criminal matters and possibly a consular convention.
FIVE AIRPORT PROJECTS SPOTTED FOR PRIVATE INVESTMENT

The Ministry of Civil Aviation has identified five pilot projects at Delhi, Bombay, Madras, Calcutta and Ahmedabad airports for 100 percent private sector investment on a build- operate-transfer (BOT) basis. According to sources, these projects are part of the new policy on private investment in airports being framed by the ministry.
TATAS TO GET PIR PAU JETTY CONTRACT

The contract for a two million tonne coal-cum-chemical jetty at Pir Pau, off Bombay harbour, will be awarded to the Tata industrial group at a port trust board meeting on Wednesday. The Tata Electric Companies (TEC) has become the only qualified bidder for the project, estimated to cost around 2.0 billion rupees. Three other parties including the Reliance group and ABG Industries, which had acquired tender documents, did not bid for the project.
